title: every-datarecorder-declares-when-it-was-started-last-read-and-how-often-it-expects-reading
sorted_berth: none, because the node stands at THINKME — the design names are Akien's to settle (see intent_berth); /sorted fires once he has
intention: Every datarecorder carries when it started, when it was last read, how often it expects to be read, and whether it drains or reports-and-holds — so an unread recorder raises a trouble by itself instead of waiting to be noticed.
why: A datarecorder nobody reads accumulates silently — the same shape as the inspector findings that 'accumulated silently' until today. Akien 2026-09-04: with started/lastread/expected_read_frequency on every recorder, 'we can also automatically issue trouble tickets on unread data recorders.' The lived symptom is data written for a reader who never comes, discovered by accident.
how: First cut only, names undecided (Akien: 'all specifiers are ideas not decided names'): a small metadata record beside each recorder's folder under the holder's instance home; readers stamp lastread through the recorder's door; the at-rest probe on the beat compares now - lastread against the expected frequency and raises a trouble over the bus. cairn owns folder-based recorders (press_office is the exemplar). Stands at THINKME until the four names and the drain/hold switch are his.
falsifier: DONE when a recorder deliberately left unread past its declared frequency raises a trouble on the next beat, and a recorder read on time does not. WRONG INTENT if most recorders have no meaningful reader cadence — then the switch (drain vs hold) is the whole feature and the frequency is noise.
traces_to: Law 7 — an unread record is a silent error; Law 3 — 'expected read frequency' makes the claim that something is read measurable. Law 10 — the recorder can measure its own reading.
owner: cairn device owns folder-based datarecorders (press_office is one); the field names are Akien's to settle before /sorted
